description: How legacy giants fell and an EV upstart seized the crown — company market caps (year-end) 2000–2025, in billions USD. One titan rockets while another collapses.

The Auto Throne: Market cap race, 2000–2025 (year-end, billions USD).

Chapters:
0:00 Intro — The throne and the contenders
0:35 2000–2007 — Legacy ascendancy: Toyota, VW, GM, Ford
1:30 2008 crash & 2009 shocks — GM bankrupt, mass revaluation
2:20 2010–2014 — Recovery and consolidation, Tesla IPO (2010)
3:10 2015–2019 — EVs ignite; Tesla builds momentum
4:00 2020 — Pandemic market shock and the EV mania
4:40 2021 — Tesla hits the $1T crown (peak)
5:10 2022–2024 — Correction and recovery across the field
5:40 2025 — Where the throne sits now (includes 2025 estimates)
6:05 Outro & sources

Story summary:
This animation tracks the year-end market capitalizations of five automotive giants (Toyota, GM, Ford, Volkswagen, Tesla) from 2000 through 2025 in billions USD. The chart tells a dramatic story: legacy manufacturers (Toyota, VW, GM, Ford) dominate the early 2000s; the 2008 financial crisis slices valuations, culminating in GM's 2009 bankruptcy (old GM effectively 0 at year-end 2009). Tesla — effectively $0 before its 2010 IPO — emerges slowly then explodes after Model S/Model 3 scale and investor re-rating, peaking around a $1,000B market cap in 2021. The dataset shows the crash-and-restructure of GM, Ford's roller-coaster, Volkswagen's Dieselgate & rebound, Toyota's steadier line, and Tesla's meteoric rise and subsequent corrections. 2025 entries are reasonable, conservative estimates informed by late-2023/2024 market trends and company reports and are explicitly marked as estimates in this description.

Sources & notes:
- Company annual reports and filings (Toyota, GM, Ford, Volkswagen, Tesla)
- Exchange historical market caps aggregated (year-end snapshots)
- Public market reporting and major business news (2008 financial crisis, GM bankruptcy 2009, Tesla IPO 2010, Tesla peak 2021, chip shortages 2021–2022, EV adoption trends)
- 2025 values flagged as estimates/projections based on available 2023–2024 market data

instagram_caption:
🚘 The $1T Throne: how an EV upstart stole the crown from century-old giants

A decade ago the global auto industry looked stable: Toyota, Volkswagen, GM and Ford sat atop a $100B+ empire. Our animation maps year-end market caps from 2000–2025 in billions USD — and the arc is brutal. In 2008 the financial crisis punctured valuations; by 2009 GM hit zero on our chart after bankruptcy and restructuring. That collapse rewired expectations about legacy manufacturers.

Then Tesla appears. Starting near $0 at IPO in 2010, Tesla’s march is steady until the 2010s accelerate into mania: Model S credibility, the Model 3 scaling, and investors betting on electrification send Tesla from single-digit billions to a staggering $400B by 2020 and a peak around $1,000B in 2021. Meanwhile Toyota steadies, VW rebounds after Dieselgate, and Ford oscillates between restructuring hopes and market dips.

The drama isn’t just numbers. Every spike and drop lines up with real events: GM’s 2009 restructuring, Tesla’s production milestones (Model S → Model 3 → mass-market push), the pandemic-fueled market surge in 2020, and the 2022 correction as supply chains and interest-rate shifts hit valuations. By 2024–2025 the field reshapes again: Tesla still towers on our chart, legacy names regain strength but the throne has shifted.
